title: Picard-trivial automorphisms fix the normalized branches of an integral nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $Y/k$ be an integral projective curve having only nodes [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-kun-projective, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], and let $
u:\widetilde Y	o Y$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization]. Then $\widetilde Y$ is a smooth projective connected curve. Define $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ to consist of the invertible sheaf classes [def-sc-invertible-module] of degree zero after pullback to $\widetilde Y$; on $\widetilde Y$ use ordinary degree zero. Every $k$-automorphism $b$ of $Y$ has a unique lift $\widetilde b$ to $\widetilde Y$ with $
u\widetilde b=b
u$. If $b^*$ is the identity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$, then $\widetilde b^*$ is the identity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\widetilde Y)$ and $\widetilde b$ fixes individually every point of $
u^{-1}(\operatorname{Sing}Y)$. More precisely, $
u^*:\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)	o\operatorname{Pic}^0(\widetilde Y)$ is surjective, and for each node $q$ with an ordering $(p_q^-,p_q^+)$ of its two inverse images, gluing the trivial sheaf with scalar $z\in k^*$ at $q$, and scalar $1$ at all other nodes, defines an injective homomorphism $j_{q,(p_q^-,p_q^+)}:k^*	o\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$. All these homomorphisms, including the two opposite orderings at each node, are pairwise distinct, and pullback by $b$ permutes them according to its action on the ordered inverse-image pairs.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 1.15, printed p.85, ordered-branch gluing homomorphisms. Stacks curves.tex Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, iterated over self-nodes. No genus bound is needed for this normalization assertion. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $Y$ is proper. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-completed-normalization-model]: an integral curve is nonempty, reduced and pure one-dimensional, and its nodes have the completed rings stipulated there. Write $E=\operatorname{Sing}Y$. We obtain finite $E$, finite normalization, two distinct $k$-points $p_e^-,p_e^+$ over each $e$, and an isomorphism away from $E$. The normalization of an integral scheme is integral: its affine rings are the integral closures inside its single function field, hence domains, with the same generic point, by [def-sc-normalization]. Thus it has one connected component. The cited completed-model statement makes this component a smooth projective connected curve.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), normalization setup; split branches also Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node).

proof.text:
Construct the lift directly from [def-sc-normalization]. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$, $b$ identifies $b^{-1}U$ with $U$ and their fraction fields. Applying the field isomorphism to a monic equation identifies their integral-closure rings; its inverse does the reverse. These maps commute with restrictions and so define an isomorphism $\widetilde b$ with $
u\widetilde b=b
u$. Any other lift has the same function-field map, since $
u$ is the identity there. The integral-closure rings inject into this field, so its affine maps coincide with these. This proves uniqueness among all lifts. In particular $\widetilde b$ takes the pair over $e$ to the pair over $b(e)$.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), affine integral-closure construction, directly applied to isomorphisms.

proof.text: Fix $e\in E$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,e}$, $B=(\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde Y})_e$. By [lem-sfb-nodal-completed-normalization-model], $A$ is Noetherian and $B\otimes_A\widehat A=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$, with the two residues given by constant terms. The complex $0\to A\to B\xrightarrow{d_e}k\to0$, $d_e(h)=h(p_e^+)-h(p_e^-)$, becomes exact after completion: its kernel is the pairs with equal constant terms, precisely the image of $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$, and $(0,c)$ maps to $c$. Completion is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies each homology defect after tensoring with that of the completed complex; [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] makes each original defect zero. Also $\mathfrak m_AB$ is the ideal of the two reduced points: after completion both it and the kernel of $B\to k\times k$ become $(u)\times(v)$. Their quotient is zero by the same flatness and zero-reflection argument. Away from $E$, $\nu$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C1J (example-glue-points), additive difference sequence; Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node); descent from the cited completed model.

proof.text: Give $Z=\coprod_{e\in E}\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow Y$ its reduced structure. Step 3 identifies $Z'=\widetilde Y\times_YZ$ with the two reduced branch points per node and identifies $\mathcal O_Y$ with normalized functions whose paired residues agree. This verifies the affine fibre-product hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-pinching-invertible-patching]. Explicitly, for affine $U\subset Y$, put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$, $A'=\Gamma(\nu^{-1}U,\mathcal O)$, $B'=\prod_{e\in E\cap U}k$, $F=\prod_{e\in E\cap U}(k\times k)$. Then $R=A'\times_FB'$ by the equality of sheaves in Step 3, with $B'\to F$ diagonal in each pair. The map $A'\to F$ is surjective: the branch maximal ideals are pairwise comaximal; for each branch $p$ multiply elements that are $1$ modulo its ideal and $0$ modulo each other branch ideal, then sum these products with the desired residues. The cited equivalence, eliminating the line on each node, now describes a line bundle on $Y$ by a line bundle $M$ on $\widetilde Y$ and isomorphisms $\lambda_e:M_{p_e^-}\to M_{p_e^+}$. Morphisms are isomorphisms of $M$ commuting with every $\lambda_e$; tensor multiplies identifications.

source.place: Tag 0D2J (lemma-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product), applied by the cited pinching lemma; curves.tex Tag 0C1J (example-glue-points).

proof.text: For any line bundle $M$ on $\widetilde Y$, choose a nonzero vector in each of its finitely many branch fibres. These are one-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, so the selected vectors give the $\lambda_e$ of Step 4 and a line bundle $L$ on $Y$ with $\nu^*L\simeq M$. Thus pullback is surjective on Picard groups. If $M$ has degree zero then this same $L$ is in $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ by its definition in the statement. This proves the asserted surjectivity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0$, without passing from a sheaf epimorphism to rational points.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), surjectivity, explicitly obtained from Step 4.

proof.text: Take $M=\mathcal O_{\widetilde Y}$ and let $\lambda_e$ be multiplication by $a_e\in k^*$. Step 4 gives a homomorphism $J:(k^*)^E\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$: pullback is trivial and tensor multiplies parameters. By [lem-sc-global-functions], every automorphism of $\mathcal O_{\widetilde Y}$ is multiplication by a single $c\in k^*$, since $\widetilde Y$ is reduced, proper and connected. An isomorphism from the data $(a_e)$ to $(a'_e)$ must satisfy $ca_e=a'_ec$ for every $e$, forcing $a_e=a'_e$. Conversely equal tuples give equal data. Hence $J$ is injective, and its coordinate homomorphism at $e$ is exactly $j_{e,(p_e^-,p_e^+)}$ of the statement.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), global-unit quotient and injectivity on the same proper connected component.

proof.text: Reversing the ordering at $e$ replaces $\lambda_e$ by its inverse, so the opposite-ordering map is $z\mapsto J((1,\ldots,z^{-1},\ldots,1))$. Choose a root $z$ of $T^3-T-1$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Then $z(z^2-1)=1$, so $z\in k^*$ and $z\ne z^{-1}$ in every characteristic. Injectivity of $J$ distinguishes the two maps at one node by evaluation at $z$, and distinguishes maps at different nodes by their different nontrivial coordinates, regardless of ordering. All the homomorphisms in the statement are therefore pairwise distinct.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), scalar gluing; direct coordinate calculation of distinct ordered-branch maps.

proof.text:
Pulling back the gluing data by $b$ places scalar $z$ at $(\widetilde b^{-1}p_e^-,\widetilde b^{-1}p_e^+)$ over $b^{-1}e$ and scalar $1$ elsewhere: pull back the two fibre maps, using that $b$ fixes $k$ and that the trivial normalized sheaf has its canonical section $1$. Thus
$$b^*j_{e,(p_e^-,p_e^+)}=j_{b^{-1}e,(\widetilde b^{-1}p_e^-,\widetilde b^{-1}p_e^+)}.$$
The two bundles are identified by the fully faithful pullback equivalence of [lem-sfb-finite-pinching-invertible-patching], since their pulled-back triples agree. If $b^*$ is the identity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$, Step 7 forces this ordered pair to equal $(p_e^-,p_e^+)$. This fixes both points individually for every node.

source.place: Tag 0C1J (example-glue-points), pullback of branch identifications; explicit contravariant permutation.

proof.text:
An isomorphism of proper curves preserves degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]: its pullback equivalence identifies each coherent cohomology vector space, hence their alternating dimensions. Thus $b^*$ and $\widetilde b^*$ preserve the degree-zero groups in the statement. For $[M]\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(\widetilde Y)$, choose $[L]\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ mapping to it by Step 5. From $
u\widetilde b=b
u$ and composition of module pullbacks,
$$\widetilde b^*[M]=\widetilde b^*
u^*[L]=
u^*b^*[L]=
u^*[L]=[M].$$
This proves the remaining assertion. If $E$ is empty, all gluing data are empty, all branch claims are vacuous, and the same argument applies.

source.place: Tag 0AYR (definition-degree-invertible-sheaf), invariance under isomorphism and pullback composition; agent assembly.
